lookback_source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

lookback_notes: I5200 is one of the checkboxes in the I0100–I8000 "Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days" section. The document states two look-back periods for this section: diagnosis identification (Step 1) uses a 60-day look-back for the physician-documented diagnosis, and diagnosis status (active/inactive, Step 2) uses a 7-day look-back. The assessor's observation window for determining active status is 7 days; the 60-day window governs identification of the physician-documented diagnosis. The document does not state on these pages how the 7-day window is counted relative to the ARD.

coding_levels.label: I5200 Multiple Sclerosis (MS) — checked
coding_levels.definition: Check the I5200 box when multiple sclerosis is an active disease, i.e., a diagnosis documented in the last 60 days that has a direct relationship to the resident's current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Check off each active disease. Check all that apply.

coding_levels.label: I5200 Multiple Sclerosis (MS) — not checked
coding_levels.definition: Leave unchecked when the condition is not active; the document instructs: "Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the resident's plan of care during the 7-day look-back period, as these would be considered inactive diagnoses."

source.quote: Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the resident's plan of care during the 7-day look-back period, as these would be considered inactive diagnoses.

federal_coding_rules.rule: I5200 is the Neurological-category checkbox for multiple sclerosis (MS) within items I0100–I8000, Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

source.quote: I5200, multiple sclerosis (MS)

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code diseases that have a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days AND have a direct relationship to the resident's current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Code diseases that have a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days and have a direct relationship to the resident's current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period

federal_coding_rules.rule: The diagnosis must be physician-documented (or documented by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) within the last 60 days.

source.quote: Identify diagnoses: The disease conditions in this section require a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Once the diagnosis is identified, the assessor must determine whether it is active; do not code conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the plan of care during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the resident's plan of care during the 7-day look-back period, as these would be considered inactive diagnoses.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check all that apply — each active disease is checked off; multiple diagnosis checkboxes may be coded on the same assessment.

source.quote: Check off each active disease. Check all that apply.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the primary medical condition coded in I0020B is multiple sclerosis, it must also be included (checked) in items I0100–I8000.

source.quote: Include the primary medical condition coded in item I0020B in items I0100–I8000: Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Listing the diagnosis on the resident's medical record problem list alone is not sufficient to determine active or inactive status.

source.quote: Listing a disease/diagnosis (e.g., arthritis) on the resident's medical record problem list is not sufficient for determining active or inactive status.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Routine nursing monitoring of medications for adverse effects does not by itself establish active disease; for coding purposes that monitoring relates to management of pharmacotherapy, not to management or monitoring of the underlying disease.

source.quote: It is expected that nurses monitor all medications for adverse effects as part of usual nursing practice. For coding purposes, this monitoring relates to management of pharmacotherapy and not to management or monitoring of the underlying disease.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Where a practitioner has potentially misdiagnosed the resident and appropriate diagnostic information is lacking in the medical record, the corresponding Section I diagnosis should not be coded.

source.quote: In situations where practitioners have potentially misdiagnosed residents with a condition for which there is a lack of appropriate diagnostic information in the medical record, such as for a mental disorder, the corresponding diagnosis in Section I should not be coded

federal_coding_rules.rule: If aftercare following hospitalization is coded with a Z code, another diagnosis for the related primary medical condition must still be checked in items I0100–I7900 or entered in I8000.

source.quote: When Z codes are used, another diagnosis for the related primary medical condition should be checked in items I0100–I7900 or entered in I8000.

federal.criterion: A physician-documented diagnosis of multiple sclerosis dated within the last 60 days; acceptable medical record sources include progress notes, the most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, and the diagnosis/problem list (problem-list entries only if confirmed by the physician).

source.quote: Medical record sources for physician diagnoses include progress notes, the most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, diagnosis/ problem list, and other resources as available. If a diagnosis/problem list is used, only diagnoses confirmed by the physician should be entered.

federal.criterion: Diagnoses communicated verbally by the physician must be documented in the medical record by the physician.

source.quote: it is also essential that diagnoses communicated verbally be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure follow-up

federal.criterion: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must be documented in the medical record by the physician.

source.quote: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must also be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure validity and follow-up.

federal.criterion: Evidence of active status must be sought in medical record sources covering the last 7 days: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor's orders, consults and official diagnostic reports.

source.quote: Check the following information sources in the medical record for the last 7 days to identify "active" diagnoses: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor's orders, consults and official diagnostic reports, and other sources as available.

federal.criterion: Specific documentation by a physician, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist that the condition is active (e.g., in progress notes, most recent history and physical, transfer notes, hospital discharge summary) is sufficient and requires no additional confirmation.

source.quote: There may be specific documentation in the medical record by a physician, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist of active diagnosis.

federal.notes: Framed as an indicator that "may assist assessors"; documentation of active status is nonetheless the basis for coding.

federal.criterion: In the absence of specific documentation that the disease is active: documentation of recent onset or acute exacerbation indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms, and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days (sources: radiological reports, hospital discharge summaries, doctor's orders).

source.quote: Recent onset or acute exacerbation of the disease or condition indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days.

federal.criterion: Documentation of symptoms and abnormal signs indicating ongoing or decompensated disease in the last 7 days, with the symptom specifically attributed to the disease (sources: radiological reports, nursing assessments and care plans, progress notes).

source.quote: Symptoms and abnormal signs indicating ongoing or decompensated disease in the last 7 days.

federal.notes: The document adds: "a symptom must be specifically attributed to the disease."

federal.criterion: Documentation of ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions in the last 7 days that manage the condition and require monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or for potentially severe side effects.

source.quote: Ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions to manage a condition that requires monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or to monitor potentially severe side effects in the last 7 days.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied pages do not tie I5200 to any payment or case-mix classification. (I0020, a separate item, references the Medicare Part A stay, but no such statement is made for I5200 or the I0100–I8000 checkboxes.)

conflicts.topic: Two coexisting time windows for Section I active diagnoses (60-day diagnosis identification vs. 7-day active status)

positions.claim: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) uses a 60-day look-back period.

source.quote: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) is a 60-day look-back period.

positions.claim: Diagnosis status (active or inactive, Step 2) uses a 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document itself: it explicitly states there are two look-back periods for this section — 60 days to identify the physician-documented diagnosis and 7 days to determine active status. Both must be met to check I5200.
